module_title: Municipalities - 8 Types of Urban Governments and Central Control
introduction: This advanced level explores the 8 different types of urban local bodies in India, highlighting that not all urban areas are governed by the 74th Amendment. We specifically focus on bodies like Cantonment Boards, which operate under Central Government laws rather than State laws.

core_concepts.title: 8 Types of Urban Local Bodies
core_concepts.description: 1. Municipal Corporation, 2. Municipality, 3. Notified Area Committee, 4. Town Area Committee, 5. Cantonment Board, 6. Township, 7. Port Trust, 8. Special Purpose Agency.

core_concepts.title: Cantonment Board
core_concepts.description: Established for municipal administration for civilian populations in cantonment areas. Unlike other urban bodies, it is created by a Central Act (Cantonment Act, 2006) and works under the administrative control of the Union Ministry of Defence.

core_concepts.title: Notified Area Committee & Town Area Committee
core_concepts.description: A Notified Area Committee is created for a fast-developing town or a town lacking preconditions for a municipality. It is entirely nominated by the State Government (no elections). A Town Area Committee is for small towns, mainly doing limited civic functions.

core_concepts.title: The 12th Schedule (Article 243W)
core_concepts.description: It contains 18 functional items placed within the purview of municipalities, such as urban planning, regulation of land use, public health, fire services, and urban poverty alleviation.

core_concepts.title: Port Trusts
core_concepts.description: Established in port areas like Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai to manage and protect the ports and provide civic amenities. They are created by an Act of Parliament.

important_entities.name: General Officer Commanding (GOC)
important_entities.significance: A Cantonment Board consists of partly elected and partly nominated members. The military officer commanding the station acts as its President, highlighting the defense-civic overlap.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Cantonment Boards are NOT under State Government
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A major trap in UPSC exams. While Municipal Corporations and Councils are created by State Legislatures and fall under the State Government, Cantonment Boards are created by Parliament and fall under the Central Government (Ministry of Defence).

Do not assume all local bodies have elections. A Notified Area Committee is an entirely nominated body. The State government nominates all its members; thus, it is neither an elected nor a statutory body.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Panchayats have a wider scope of local functions (29 items in the 11th Schedule) compared to Municipalities (18 items in the 12th Schedule).

exam_strategy_tips: In Assertion-Reasoning questions, always isolate Cantonment Boards and Port Trusts as bodies established by Central Acts (Parliament) rather than State Acts.

Understand the distinction between a Municipal Corporation (has more autonomy, deals with larger areas directly under the State Govt) and a Municipality (deals with smaller towns, controlled through the District Collector).
